MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 22, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED - VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  9:00A.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Cherin called the meeting to order at 9:04 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lotte Cherin; Vice Chair Holland (arrived at 9:07 a.m.); Commissioners
  Barry Haldeman, and Fireball Lawrence; and Ex-Officio Clifford (arrived at 9:07 a.m.)

  ABSENT: Commissioner Peter Jones

  ALSO PRESENT: Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Deputy Director; and Kate Gallo, Recreation Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Cherin led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CITY OF MALIBU VISION STATEMENT

  None.

  At 9:07 a.m., Vice Chair Holland and Ex-Officio Clifford joined the meeting.

  At 9:08 a.m., Chair Cherin left and re-joined the meeting due to technical issues.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Haldeman moved, and Chair Cherin seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner
  Jones absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA
   Malibu A1is Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 2 of7

  Recreation Manager Gallo repo1ied the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  March 17, 2022.

ITEMl  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  I.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops took
  place at Malibu Elementary School, Malibu Middle School, and Malibu
  High School. She stated staff was editing the Student Anthology which
  would be released in June 2022.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Vice Chair Holland stated photographs for the "Malibu Perception"
  photography exhibition would be reviewed by her and Commissioner
  Lawrence. She stated she would meet with Poet Laureate Ann Buxie to
  discuss the addition of poetry for upcoming exhibitions.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Vice Chair Holland stated specific artists were
  selected by the Ad Hoc for the exhibition.

  Chair Cherin stated she preferred to have a Call for Artists for community
  mi exhibitions and have the submissions juried by an outside panel instead
  of Commissioners.

  Commissioner Lawrence indicated disagreement with Chair Cherin. He
  stated photographers included in the exhibition were well-known Malibu
  artists. He stated the Commission discussed selecting specific artists rather
  than holding a Call for Artists when the a1i exhibition schedule was
  originally reviewed and approved.

  Vice Chair Holland stated atiists were selected based on their paiiicipation
  in previous exhibitions.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Commissioner Lawrence stated
  the Commission discussed the exhibition schedule and details multiple
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 3 of7

  times. He stated delaying the exhibition to conduct a Call for Artists would
  affect the exhibition schedule.

  Ex-Officio Clifford stated the exhibition should move forward as planned.
  He stated the desire to coordinate an outside jury and a Call for A1iists
  should have been expressed before the exhibition was planned to open.

  Vice Chair Holland stated the summer surf exhibition would have a Call for
  A1tists.

  Commissioner Lawrence stated the Ad Hoc had completed two exhibitions
  and hoped the Commission would trust their judgment when curating
  exhibitions.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the Malibu Chamber of Commerce had
  prepared an Art in Business proposal which the Ad Hoc Committee was
  reviewing. He stated the Chamber requested aitist recommendations from
  the Commission to include in the Art in Business proposal.

  In response to Community Services Director Bobbett, Commissioner
  Haldeman stated he did not know the extent of City support the Malibu
  Chamber of Commerce was requesting. He stated the Chamber would ask
  for assistance with advertising gallery openings.

  4.  Social Media

  Commissioner Lawrence stated staff had been consistently posting on the
  Malibu Arts Commission Facebook page.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Commissioner Lawrence seconded a motion to approve
  the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Jones absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  I.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the February 22, 2022
  Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 4 of7

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu Atts Budget
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Malibu Arts Budget for Fiscal Year 2022-
  2023; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff rep0tt.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Director Bobbett stated the Art
  in Public Places Fund was separate from the General Fund and did not fluctuate
  based on the City's budget. He stated the only qualifying project under the Arts in
  Public Places Ordinance that had contributed to the Art in Public Places Fund was
  the Whole Foods development.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Community Services Director Bobbett stated
  the draft arts budget was prepared by staff and reflected expenditures for
  programming, events, marketing, and staffing.

  Commissioner Haldeman suggested adding $35,000 to the draft arts budget for a
  publicist. He stated an additional $500 was needed for the At1 in Business program
  for community outreach and marketing.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Deputy Director
  Riesgo stated the annual website domain fee was included in the budget.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Director Bobbett stated costs for
  a community survey were included in the draft arts budget.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director Bobbett
  recommended the Commission research costs for an Arts Center consultant and
  request the City Council approve funding once the research was completed.

  Commissioner Lawrence stated a concept design would be required before the
  Commission could move forward with the At1s Center.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Commissioner Lawrence.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Community Services Director Bobbett stated he would
  include the costs for an Arts Center consultant requested by the Commission in the
  budget, but he needed detailed information regarding the request.

  Chair Cherin suggested adding $15,000 to the draft arts budget for research and
  development of an Atts Center.

  B.  Malibu Performing Arts Center
  Recommended Action: Discuss ideas for a performing arts center in Malibu.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 5 of7

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff rep01i.

  John Johannessen provided a brief background about himself and his mission to
  help create a concept design for an arts center. He stated he worked with Ed Niles
  to develop the idea and a conceptual model.

  Commissioner Lawrence stated he was interested in seeing the model and providing
  revisions to fit the community's needs for an arts center.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Commissioner Lawrence.

  Mr. Johannessen suggested adding a theater with a multi-purpose space as part of
  the proposed arts center. He stated Malibu City Hall does not have a space that
  allowed guests to dine-in the same room as the theater.

  Chair Cherin requested Mr. Johannessen and the Commission to provide a list of
  arts center community survey questions to staff.

C.  Malibu Mermaid Sculpture Donation
  Recommended Action: At the request of Commissioner Lawrence, review the
  proposed donation of the Malibu Mermaid sculpture.

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Commissioner Lawrence stated it would
  cost $6,000 to bronze the sculpture and there would be an additional cost for the
  base. He stated he wanted to incorporate a story, meaning, and experience with the
  Malibu Mermaid sculpture.

  Vice Chair Holland stated she was in favor of accepting the sculpture donation.

  Commissioner Haldeman stated he wanted to know the engineering cost before
  accepting the donation. He stated the Commission should consider other sculpture
  donations before accepting the Malibu Mermaid sculpture.

  Commissioner Lawrence rec used himself from the discussion.

  At l 0:39 a.m., Commissioner Lawrence left the meeting.

  Ex-Officio Clifford stated the sculpture should be displayed in a sculpture garden.
  He indicated support for the City paying for the installation and the artist paying
  for the bronzing. He stated accepting the sculpture was a conflict of interest because
  it was created by a Commissioner's wife, would be permanently installed, and had
  no backstory or meaning to Malibu.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 6 of7

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Ex-Officio Clifford.

  Chair Cherin stated she was not in favor of accepting the sculpture donation.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission decided not to move forward with the proposed
  donation of the Malibu Mermaid sculpture.

  D.  City Hall Art Exhibitions
  Recommended Action: At the request of Chair Cherin, discuss the proposed
  Hollywood-themed City Hall Art Exhibition with featured artist Alexander
  Golitsyn for the Fiscal Year 2022-2023.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Chair Cherin provided background information
  on Alexander Golitsyn and his work as a production designer.

  Ex-Officio Clifford stated he preferred curating a Hollywood-themed exhibition
  with multiple artists, including Mr. Golitsyn' s artwork.

  Vice Chair Holland indicated agreement with Ex-Officio Clifford.

  Commissioner Haldeman suggested incorporating movie stills into the exhibition.

  Vice Chair Holland suggested working with the Malibu Film Society for the
  Hollywood-themed exhibition.

  Ex-Officio Clifford indicated agreement with Vice Chair Holland. He stated the
  annual theme could highlight various movie aspects including feature production
  designs, and he offered his assistance with the exhibition.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission agreed to curate a Hollywood-themed art
  exhibition, incorporating artwork by Alexander Golitsyn.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo provided an update on upcoming art
  events.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 7 of7

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the Malibu Film Society did not have a facility to
  host events in Malibu and had to coordinate events outside of Malibu. He requested
  Commission support for the Malibu Film Society to host film screenings in Malibu.

  Chair Cherin and Ex-Officio Clifford indicated agreement with Commissioner
  Haldeman.

  Ex-Officio Clifford stated he could not attend the April 26, 2022 Regular meeting.

  At 11 :01 a.m., Vice Chair Holland and Ex-Officio Clifford left the meeting.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Malibu Performing Arts Center
  Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Commission Work Plan
  Malibu Film Society Endorsement

ADJOURNMENT

  At 11: IO a.m., the meeting adjourned due to a lack of a quorum.
